cash_flow_atoms.note: The 4 atoms for scripts/db/_apply_conventions.py ATOM dict, in US$'000 (native currency, no FX). Format (dep_pe, fv_cf_signed, finance_costs, capex_sum):

detail.basis: P&E depreciation: no depreciation line in C/F operating activities (pure-IP REIT) = 0. Net FV change of IP: C/F operating line 'Net change in fair value of investment properties' = (251,601) i.e. -251,601 (P&L gain of +251,601 added back/subtracted in C/F, p156). Gross finance costs: Note 17 finance-costs total 25,122 (NOT netted against finance income 11,107). IP capex: C/F investing 'Additions to investment properties' = 10,766 (p156); EXCLUDES 'Acquisition of a subsidiary' 55,077 (Frankfurt) and 'Investment in associates' 166,159 (Osaka/Frankfurt associate step-ups), matching the DCRU FY2025 precedent where capex = IP additions only. The Financial Review (p32) confirms 'US$10.8m for capital expenditure' as a distinct line from the acquisition outflows.

derived_metrics_computed.note: Populated per REFERENCE.md §6 LOCKED formulas from the atoms above (full USD units).
derived_metrics_computed.depreciation_basis: = P&E depreciation (0) + net FV change of IP C/F-signed (-251,601)
derived_metrics_computed.ebitda_basis: = pretax_income 305,471 + interest 25,122 + depreciation (-251,601) = 78,992 (strips the non-cash revaluation gain, SG-REIT EBITDA convention)
derived_metrics_computed.ffo_basis: = net_income 265,450 + depreciation (-251,601) - net_property_sales (0) = 13,849. FFO legitimately falls far below net income in a big revaluation-gain year (NAREIT).
